# Measure Commands

Every command the `measure` module offers, from its declarations, in order of the resource each acts on. Each command's help says the same.

## Export

### `lnk measure export set`

Send every look to an OTLP endpoint too (an OpenTelemetry collector, Grafana, Honeycomb), or stop: one of --url, --off, or --job

```usage
lnk measure export set [--header-file <header-file>] [--job <job>] [--json] [--off] [--url <url>]
```

- `--header-file`, path: A file of headers sent with each look, `name: value` a line (an API key), or `-` for standard input; kept only for you to read
- `--job`, string: Send one retained job profile to the configured endpoint and wait for its acknowledgement
- `--json`, boolean: Print the answer as JSON for other programs
- `--off`, boolean: Stop sending looks
- `--url`, string: Its OTLP/HTTP address (`http://localhost:4318`; looks go to `<url>/v1/metrics`, as JSON)

It answers `core.report`.

## Measure

### `lnk measure get`

Show how often the watcher looks, how long it keeps what it saw, and where else it sends it: yours, and Link's where you set none

```usage
lnk measure get [--json]
```

It takes `--json`, boolean: Print the answer as JSON for other programs. It answers `core.report`.

### `lnk measure list`

What your agents and this machine use: memory, CPU, disk, network, tokens, spend

```usage
lnk measure list [--agent <agent>] [--job <job>] [--json] [--pid <pid>]
```

- `--agent`, string: One agent, now and over the last day, an hour at a time, by its name (`lnk agent list`) [default: this machine, as a tree]
- `--job`, string: A retained job profile and its child stages, by job ID
- `--json`, boolean: Print the answer as JSON for other programs
- `--pid`, integer: One process of that agent, by its ID

It answers `measure.measured`.

### `lnk measure set`

Set how often the watcher looks, and how long it keeps what it saw, then show them all: yours, and Link's where you set none

```usage
lnk measure set [--every <every>] [--folders-every <folders-every>] [--folders-max <folders-max>] [--json] [--keep-fine <keep-fine>] [--keep-minutes <keep-minutes>] [--no-processes] [--processes]
```

- `--every`, string: How often it looks (`10s`, `1m`)
- `--folders-every`, string: How often each agent's folders are walked for their size (`10m`)
- `--folders-max`, integer: The most entries a walk of an agent's folders counts
- `--json`, boolean: Print the answer as JSON for other programs
- `--keep-fine`, string: How long every look is kept (`12h`, `1d`)
- `--keep-minutes`, string: How long each minute's summary is kept, after (`30d`)
- `--no-processes`, boolean: Keep each agent's processes no more
- `--processes`, boolean: Keep each agent's processes too: about seven times the disk

It answers `core.report`.

### `lnk measure show`

Show this execution's CPU, memory and filesystem capacity, including usable container limits. Missing observations stay unknown.

```usage
lnk measure show [--json] [--path <path>]
```

It takes `--json`, boolean: Print the answer as JSON for other programs. It takes `--path`, path: Observe filesystem capacity for this directory (default: the current directory), as well as temporary storage. It answers `measure.capacity`.

### `lnk measure start`

Keep watching in the background: a look every so often (`lnk measure set`), kept on this machine

```usage
lnk measure start [--json] [--quiet]
```

It takes `--json`, boolean: Print the answer as JSON for other programs. It takes `--quiet`, boolean: Say less, for another of Link's commands running it on the way. It answers `core.report`.

### `lnk measure stop`

Stop watching in the background; what it kept stays

```usage
lnk measure stop [--json]
```

It takes `--json`, boolean: Print the answer as JSON for other programs. It answers `core.report`.
